title: HomeView Tidbits: Mirror, Sleep Timer, and Other Details
content:
Apple's HomeView is out today, and we're finally learning all the little details about the new hub. We've rounded up a list of tidbits for those setting up a HomeView or thinking about getting one.


Sunglasses

Apple says the HomeView probably won't recognize you if you have your face covered, including when wearing sunglasses. If HomeView isn't identifying you, Apple suggests removing anything that would block the camera from seeing your face.

The HomeView's screen needs to be angled toward your face, you need to be centered in the frame and closest to the camera if other people are around, and the HomeView can't be blocked by overhanging shelves and cabinets. Apple says the HomeView needs front-facing, even light.
Mirror

There's a "Mirror" in the HomeView Control Center that lets you use the camera to see yourself. There's an option to turn on an edge light for face illumination, along with 1x and 2x zoom.
Guest Controls

The HomeView owner has multiple options for what guests can access.

 	
Safari can be turned on or off, or adult websites can be blocked.

 	
By default, guests can use Siri for general knowledge, writing help, and math help, but ‌Siri‌ features can be turned off.

 	
Explicit content can be turned on or off.

 	
There's an option to choose which Apple Music subscription supplies music for an unrecognized user.


Wi-Fi/Cellular

The HomeView authenticates people through face recognition and by making sure their iOS device is nearby, recently unlocked, and on the same Wi-Fi network as the HomeView. If there's a Wi-Fi outage, Apple says cellular can also be used to unlock personal content as long as it's in the same location and was recently on the Wi-Fi network.
Sleep Timer

You can set a sleep timer on HomeView to pause whatever media is playing when the timer goes off.
No Buttons

There is no button to turn the HomeView on or off, or restart it. It can be restarted from the Settings app or by briefly unplugging it.
Logins

You can log into websites and apps using your iPhone, similar to how the Apple TV works.
Notifications

The HomeView only has notifications for phone calls and home devices, with an option to toggle on critical notifications. There are no other notification settings or options.
Liquid Glass

The transparency of the Liquid Glass interface can be adjusted from clear to opaque like on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.
Personal Data Lockouts

If someone tries to repeatedly access personal content on HomeView that needs authentication, facial recognition via the camera is disabled and you'll need to prove identity with a registered device.

title: Update: Microsoft offers explanation for day-long Internet outage
content:
Macworld





Whether you’re using a Mac, iPhone, or – shudder – a PC, a major Microsoft outage has disrupted Outlook email and other Microsoft 365 services worldwide. The problems began on Thursday, November 12, and continued overnight into Friday, affecting businesses, schools and public services.
Microsoft said a server process had become overwhelmed, reducing capacity. Recovery proved difficult because some servers became unresponsive again as traffic returned. Features that depend on Exchange Online were particularly affected, although not every function within each Microsoft service stopped working.
A look at Downdetector and ThousandEyes Outages also showed complaints involving unrelated platforms. However, those reports don’t establish that every service was down or that they shared Microsoft’s underlying problem. Amazon told Macworld that AWS was operating normally. Some users also reported problems with iMessage, although Apple’s System Status page showed no corresponding outage at the time.
Microsoft reported signs of recovery as it restarted affected infrastructure and managed traffic, but had not provided a confirmed time for full restoration. The company had not established a final root cause and said there was no indication that malicious activity was responsible.
Settle in, and here’s hoping it’s fixed soon. You can track the Microsoft service health here, and we’ll keep this article updated as we learn more.


Update 8:55 pm GMT / 3:55 pm ET: Network change blamed
Microsoft has apologized for the outage as it works to restore all systems to normal: “This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.”


						

							


Update 11:45 am GMT / 6.45 am ET: Recovery underway
Microsoft says it has completed recovery actions in Asia-Pacific and this recovery work is being extended to other regions, as per the Guardian’s live blog. 


						

							


Update 10:15 am GMT / 5.15 am ET: The U.K. has woken up to the Microsoft outage
Microsoft’s service disruption continued into Friday, November 13, affecting Outlook email and Microsoft 365 features that depend on Exchange Online. 
The disruption has affected NHS communications, with reports of NHS trusts, including Evelina London, a children’s healthcare provider, unable to send or receive emails. 
Elsewhere, police forces have confirmed that some online reporting forms could be affected, but their ability to answer and respond to 999 and 101 calls had not been compromised. 
Schools have also reported communication problems and asked parents to telephone rather than email their child’s school.
Microsoft’s Friday morning advisory, via the University of Pennsylvania’s Microsoft incident-report feed, says most core Teams calling, meetings and messaging functionality is unaffected, although calendar and other email-dependent features can fail.
Microsoft reported early signs of stabilization on Friday morning, but said capacity had not returned to normal and recovery remained uneven.


						

							


Update 9:45 pm ET: “Positive results” 
Microsoft reported “seeing positive results” with its efforts to correct the outage as it restarted affected infrastructure and brought servers back into service in isolation.


						

							


Update 4:39 pm ET: AWS is normal 
An Amazon spokesperson reached out to Macworld to let us know that AWS is functioning normally and has been all day. 
Any disruptions today would have to be caused by something else.


						

							


Update 2:00 pm ET: The whole Internet is having major issues right now
Whether you’re using a Mac, iPhone, or – shudder – a PC, you may be having trouble accessing Outlook email and other Microsoft 365 services.
Downdetector and ThousandEyes Outages are recording widespread reports of connectivity problems. Users have also reported issues with unrelated platforms, although those reports do not establish that every service is down or that they share the same underlying cause.
Some users are reporting problems with Apple services, including iMessage, but Apple’s System Status page shows no corresponding outage at the time of writing.
OpenAI and Anthropic have also reported disruption to the tools that connect their AI assistants to Microsoft 365. For ChatGPT users who connect Microsoft services, this could interrupt tasks that depend on retrieving information from those services.
The cause and expected restoration time remain unclear. We’ll update this live blog as providers confirm more information.
creator: Macworld

title: Siri AI Still Not Enabled on HomePod Mini 2 With Latest Software Update
content:
Apple today released HomePod software version 27.2.1, but it does not enable Siri AI on the HomePod mini 2. Apple's website continues to say the feature is "coming in a future software update," but it has not provided a timeframe.


Due to the HomePod mini 2 having only 2GB of RAM, well below the minimum 8GB of RAM required for dedicated Siri AI, personal context requests will require a paired Apple Intelligence–enabled iPhone or iPad with Siri AI turned on. 

tvOS 27.2.1 was also released today, and it enables Siri AI on the Apple TV 4K (2nd generation) and Apple TV 4K (3rd generation). Siri AI is an opt-in feature on these devices, so after installing the update you will need to open the Settings app and tap on General → Siri → Siri AI (Beta). This will initiate a download with support.

title: Apple Releases tvOS 27.2.1 With Siri AI for Older Apple TVs
content:
Apple today released tvOS 27.2.1, an update to the tvOS 27 operating system that launched in September. tvOS 27.2.1 comes nearly three weeks after Apple released tvOS 27.2.


tvOS 27.2.1 brings Siri AI support to the 2nd- and 3rd-generation Apple TV 4K models, but it is available for all ‌Apple TV‌ 4K models that support tvOS 27.

Apple announced ‌Siri‌ AI for the ‌Apple TV‌ when debuting the 4th-generation ‌Apple TV‌ 4K. A separate tvOS 27.2 build activates ‌Siri‌ AI on the newest set-top box, but the older ‌Apple TV‌ 4K models will need the tvOS 27.2.1 update to get access.

‌Siri‌ AI is the smarter, more capable version of ‌Siri‌ that Apple introduced earlier this year. ‌Siri‌ AI can play content, draw on personal context to offer suggestions, answer world knowledge questions, and complete tasks.

Using ‌Siri‌ AI on the ‌Apple TV‌ requires a paired Apple Intelligence-compatible iOS device, which includes the iPhone 15 Pro and later.

 System > Software Update. Apple has also released a new HomePod Software 27.2.1 update for the ‌HomePod‌ and ‌HomePod‌ mini.

title: Microsoft 365 Outage Resolving After Nearly 24 Hours
content:
The ongoing Microsoft 365 outage is resolving after nearly 24 hours. The company said the underlying issue has been fixed and it is seeing "broad recovery and stability" across its services as it works to restore access to customers.


The Microsoft 365 downtime started at approximately 1 p.m. Eastern Time on Thursday. Customers could not access their Outlook email or use some features in Teams and Copilot. Exchange accounts in Apple Mail were also affected. Most calling, meeting, and messaging functions stayed online, but some users ran into errors scheduling meetings or adding calendar entries.

Businesses, educational institutions, and governments worldwide were impacted by the outage.

Microsoft apologized for the outage and said it was unrelated to a cyberattack or AI agents. It was caused by an issue introduced in an earlier network capacity upgrade. Microsoft said it will give a full incident report after completing a review.
We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.

This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.

Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration.


Just over two weeks ago, Microsoft announced plans to eliminate thousands of jobs. The company offered voluntary buyouts to 60,000 people, or a quarter of its global workforce, presumably to cut costs while its AI spending grows.

Service Health Status page still says some services may be unavailable at the current time.

title: iPhone Duo Survives 450,000 Folds, but Hinge is Weakening
content:
For the last three weeks, CNET has been stress testing the iPhone Duo's hinge on a livestream. After over 451,000 folds, the hinge is showing signs of wear.



CNET says the hinge started feeling looser at the 390,000-fold point, and by 440,300 folds, there was enough of a shift in the mechanism that the screen didn't open in full before the machine closed it again, and there was no distinctive snap. It is 5 to 10 degrees from the fully open state and can be opened fully by hand.
The wire we use to open the phone screen would withdraw before the screen was in the fully open position, but it would then sort of "coast" the rest of the way down. But between 12:30 and 1 a.m. this morning, around 440,300 folds, the screen would no longer have time to open all the way before the Fold-a-Phone caused it to close again.

The ‌iPhone Duo‌ hasn't been removed from the folding machine, and the test is continuing. CNET says the device is still operational and maintaining other screen positions, with no signs of cracking or other failure.

The site plans to continue folding the ‌iPhone Duo‌ until it hits predetermined failure conditions that include loss of power, sensors failing to detect the screen properly, and screen blackout.

Apple hasn't shared the results of ‌iPhone Duo‌ hinge testing it likely did internally, or given an estimated fold lifespan.

OLED panels sourced from Samsung Display, and Samsung's screens have undergone certified third-party fold testing. The display used for the Galaxy Z Fold7 passed a 500,000-fold durability test. Apple probably isn't using an off-the-shelf Samsung display, but CNET's testing already suggests the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s ‌OLED‌ panel is on track to match.

The combination of the display and the strength of Apple's hinge design will determine lifespan. At around 450,000 folds, the ‌iPhone Duo‌ would last over a decade at 100 folds per day.

CNET's livestream will continue until the ‌iPhone Duo‌ fails. The livestream runs on weekdays from 10 a.m. Pacific until 2 p.m. Pacific.

title: Coming to Apple TV: All the upcoming shows, movies, trailers, and more
content:
Macworld





Apple’s list of currently available content for Apple TV continues to grow, and so does the list of upcoming projects in the works.
Some of these projects have been officially announced and acknowledged by Apple, while others have been reported by the Hollywood press.
We’ve divided this list in two: Coming Soon is a list of shows and films for which Apple has given an official release date or release window, and Further Out compiles content that is still in production or perhaps haven’t even begun yet.
Updated November 13, 2026: We have updated our list with the latest release dates, images, and trailers.
How to get Apple TV
Apple TV 4K (2026)
$299 at Apple							
						
You can subscribe to Apple TV on Apple’s website here, or via the Apple TV app on your device. It costs $14.99/£9.99 a month. You can also opt for a one-year subscription for $119/£89, which effectively gives you two months free each year.
Apple also offers various trials. Take a look at our article explaining all the ways you can watch Apple TV for free, and the best Apple TV deals you can get. Students can get Apple TV for free with an already subsidized Apple Music subscription.
You don’t need an Apple TV set top box to watch Apple TV, nor do you have to pay for a subscription, see: How to watch Apple TV for free.
Coming Soon to Apple TV
The following shows, series, and movies have been officially announced by Apple and will typically will begin streaming in the next few weeks or months.
Way of the Warrior Kid
What it’s about: Middle school has been a nightmare for Marc, a good kid who’s bullied by his classmates and feels like he’s behind in everything, from academics to P.E. to just making friends. That changes when his injured Uncle Jake, a decorated Navy SEAL, comes to spend the summer and recuperate with Marc and his mom, Sarah.






Important names: Stars Chris Pratt, Jude Hill, Linda Cardellini, Levi McConaughey.
When you can watch: Way of the Warrior Kid premieres on November 25, 2026.
Bad Monkey (season 2)
What it’s about: Eager to regain his detective’s badge, Yancy finds himself embroiled in a turf war between rival criminal organizations as he navigates a variety of Florida oddballs, including an erudite mob boss, his unhinged son and a hard-edged young woman who needs Yancy’s protection.






Important names: Stars Vince Vaughn, Rob Delaney, Meredith Hagner. Produced by Bill Lawrence.
When you can watch: The second season of Bad Monkey premieres on December 2, 2026.
Fraggle Rock: A Holiday Gift
What it’s about: It’s a new Fraggle Rock holiday special.






Important names: Stars John Tartaglia, Karen Prell, Donna Kimball, and Jordan Lockhart among others.
When you can watch: Fraggle Rock: A Holiday Gift streams on December 4, 2026.
The Wanted Man
What it’s about: When organized crime boss Felix Carmichael is betrayed by someone inside his own firm and sent to the notorious Staplehurst prison, he’s forced to remember his own brutality to fight for survival. 

				
					

				
			
Apple




Important names: Stars Hugh Laurie, Thandiwe Newton, Fionn Whitehead, and Gina McKee. Written and produced by George Kay.
When you can watch: The Wanted Man premieres on January 6, 2026.
Neuromancer
What it’s about: A new 10-episode drama based on the award-winning novel of the same name by William Gibson. The series will follow a damaged, top-rung super-hacker named Case who is thrust into a web of digital espionage and high-stakes crime with his partner Molly, a razor-girl assassin with mirrored eyes, aiming to pull a heist on a corporate dynasty with untold secrets.






Important names: Stars Callum Turner, Briana Middleton, Mark Strong, and Peter Sarsgaard.
When you can watch: Neuromancer premieres on January 22, 2027.
She’s Fine
What it’s about: Fresh off a messy divorce, Heidi sets out to secure a lively second act for herself and her kids. But when she stumbles into coordinating her father’s retirement community sexcapades, Heidi is forced into an unlikely alliance with his girlfriend’s perpetually single son.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Important names: Stars Elizabeth Banks, Rob Delaney, Ted Danson, and Katey Segal.
When you can watch: She’s Fine premieres on January 27, 2026.
Fleetwood Mac: The Chain
What it’s about: Mick Fleetwood, John McVie, Christine McVie, Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks reflect on their uncompromising 50-plus-year history, from their record-breaking recordings and tours through to today.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Important names: Includes interviews with Mick Fleetwood, John McVie, Christine McVie, Lindsey Buckingham.
When you can watch: Fleetwood Mac: The Chain premieres on January 27, 2026.
Prodigies
What it’s about: From London to Tokyo by way of Virginia, this unconventional take on a romantic comedy explores ideas of potential, ambition and the universal complexities of long-term relationships. 

				
					

				
			
Apple




Important names: Stars Ayo Edebiri, Will Sharpe, Yumi Asō, and Maria Bakalova.

Further Out
These shows, series, and movies may or may not have been officially announced, and do not yet have definitive release dates. Some may debut in the next few months, others be more than a year away. It’s even possible that some of these projects will never be released.
Lance Armstrong biopic
What it’s about: Deadline reports that Apple has won the bidding war for rights to a movie about the storied cyclist Lance Armstrong.
Important names: Stars Austin Butler, directed by Edward Berger.
When you can watch: The Lance Armstrong biopic does not yet have a title or release date.

What it’s about: Per Deadline, Apple out-bid Netflix and MGM for this holiday high-concept movie about a snowman that comes alive, and will go through every stage of life in just 72 hours. The childless couple who act as his “parents” go through every parenting milestone in just three days.

What it’s about: Deadline says that Apple won the rights to produce a film from the romance book Once and Again by Rebecca Serle.

Adapted from Ryan David Jahn’s book.
Important names: Starring Patrick Brammall, adapted by writer Kris Mrksa.
When you can watch: The Dispatcher does not yet have a release date.
Speed Racer
What it’s about: A live-action series based on the beloved Japanese animated show from the ’60s. 
Important names: Will be produced by J.J. Abrams’ Bad Robot production company, with Hiram Martinez and Ron Fitzgerald as writers and showrunners.
When you can watch: Speed Racer has no release date yet.
The White Darkness
What it’s about: A limited series based on David Grann’s nonfiction book about Henry Worsley, who crossed Antarctica on foot.
Important names: Tom Hiddleston stars, Soo Hugh directs.
When you can watch: The White Darkness has no release date yet.
Untitled Negro League Baseball series
What it’s about: Follows the life and career of legendary pitcher Leroy “Satchel” Paige. 
Important names: The series is produced by Erving “Magic” Johnson, among others. It is in conjunction with the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum and MLB.
When you can watch: This series has no release date yet.
Untitled Chuck Barris drama
What it’s about: Gong Show host Chuck Barris famously claimed to be a secret CIA assassin in his autobiography Confessions of a Dangerous Mind, which was made into a feature film in 2002. A Deadline report says Apple is developing an hour-long drama series about Barris as both Gong Show host and CIA assassin.
Important names: Justin Timberlake is attached to star as Chuck Barris.
When you can watch: This series has no release date yet.  
Dolly
What it’s about: Deadline describes it as a “sci-fi courtroom drama in which a robotic ‘companion doll’ kills its owner and then shocks the world by claiming that she is not guilty and asking for a lawyer.”
Important names: Florence Pugh and Vanessa Taylor are attached to star and Drew Pearce will write the script.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Bride
What it’s about: Deadline reports that this is a genre-bending film about an engineered “ideal wife” who rejects her creator, escapes captivity, and discovers her true self.
Important names: The film will star Scarlett Johansson and will be directed by Sebastián Lelio.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Earthsound
What it’s about: A natural history documentary series that uses new audio technology and cinematic 360-degree audio to reveal untold nature stories from every continent.
Important names: It will be executive produced by Alex Williamson, and the series producer is Sam Hodgson.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Untitled Idris Elba spy thriller
What it’s about: According to Variety, this is to be a “spy movie with romance set in Africa” but little else is known about the nascent project. The report says it’s early in production. 
Important names: The film will star Idris Elba and is produced by Simon Kinberg and Audrey Chon.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Hedy Lamarr series
What it’s about: According to The Hollywood Reporter, it’s an eight-episode series about the 1930s and 40s actress and inventor Hedy Lamarr (whose frequency-hopping radio technology is still the basis for many modern wireless communications).
Important names: Gal Gadot is set to star as Lamarr, with a script written by Sarah Treem.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Where the Wild Things Are
What it’s about: Apple has struck an overall deal with The Maurice Sendak Foundation to produce shows or series based on the author’s works for children. The most famous of these, by far, is Where the Wild Things Are.
Important names: Apple is working with longtime Sendak collaborator Arthur Yorinks and his production studio Night Kitchen Studios.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Custom of the Country
What it’s about: A limited-series adaptation of the Edith Wharton novel The Custom of the Country. The novel, published in the early 20th century, is about a midwestern girl who climbs the ladder of New York high society.
Important names: The big one is Sofia Coppola, who is developing the series for Apple. No word yet on whether she will direct it.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
El Gato Negro
What it’s about: Based on Richard Dominguez’s comic book about an aging luchador who teams up with his grandson to use the El Gato Negro persona to fight crime in South Texas.
Important names: Robert Rodriguez will direct and produce, while Diego Boneta will star and also produce.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Brie Larson CIA biography series
What it’s about: A report in Variety says that Apple has made a direct-to-series order for a new drama based on the real-life experiences of CIA undercover operative Amaryllis Fox. Fox has a hot novel named Life Undercover: Coming of Age in the CIA that released in October 2019. 
Important names: Brie Larson will star and executive produce the series.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
You Think It, I’ll Say It
What it’s about:  According to Variety, Apple has ordered a 10-episode, half-hour run of a new comedy variety show. The show is inspired by Curtis Sittenfeld’s collection of short stories You Think It, I’ll Say It.
Important names: SNL alum Kristen Wiig was set to star, but pulled out citing scheduling conflicts with Wonder Woman 1984. The show is created and produced by Colleen McGuinness (30 Rock, About a Boy).
When you can watch: This project does not yet have a title or release date.

title: Binance warns of iOS 27 flaw that could expose ‘private keys and login credentials’
content:
Macworld





Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has issued a warning that recent versions of iOS have a security vulnerability that can put Apple devices “at risk.” The vulnerability can be found in iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2. Binance states that the vulnerability allows malicious software to “read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem.”
However, the vulnerability can only be exploited if the malicious software was installed outside of the App Store. In other words, the malicious app has to be installed by sideloading or by a manually signed iOS App Store Package. That’s unlikely to happen outside of the EU, where Apple allows alternative app marketplaces and installation of apps outside of the App Store. 
The current version of iOS is 27.2.1, which was released on November 9, but it is not clear if that update includes a security fix that addresses the issue. Because the issue involves an unauthorized method of software installation, Apple may not address the issue immediately.
How to protect your iPhone from malware
Sideloading apps increases your chances of security risk. Software that is available on the App Store has been vetted for security issues. To minimize the chances of inadvertently installing malware, do not sideload apps on your iPhone and only use apps from the App Store. If you do sideload apps, understand that you have increased your risk.
The easiest task to perform to secure your iPhone is to update the operating system. iOS can be updated in the Settings app by tapping General > Software Update. Apple also has a separate method for installing immediate security patches called Background Security Improvements. It is located in Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to the bottom to find Background Security Improvements. Macworld has a list of tips for keeping your iPhone secure.

Support for four-speaker ‌HomePod‌ surround sound provides another reason to consider the new ‌Apple TV‌, particularly for users who already own compatible speakers. We weigh up the appeal of expanding an existing ‌HomePod‌ setup against buying a dedicated home theater system, and consider whether these additions justify the ‌Apple TV‌'s new, higher starting price of $299.

‌Siri‌ AI is a major part of both new products, and its expanded capabilities come with familiar frustrations. title: Apple Meets Thai Officials Over iPhone Spyware Warnings
content:
Apple met with Thai officials earlier this week to discuss spyware warnings received by politicians and other users in the country, Bloomberg reports.


The discussions followed Apple's October 29 threat notifications, which reached users in 99 countries. Apple told Bloomberg that it issued the warnings after identifying activity consistent with mercenary spyware attacks, raising concerns about surveillance of Thai political figures.

Pegasus, the surveillance software made by NSO Group.

2022 investigation by Citizen Lab, working with Thai organizations iLaw and DigitalReach, confirmed infections affecting at least 30 people between October 2020 and November 2021. Those affected included activists, academics, lawyers, and others connected to the country's pro-democracy movement. Apple's warnings to Thai users in November 2021 helped initiate that investigation, with recipients contacting researchers for assistance.

issuing threat notifications since 2021, reaching users in more than 150 countries overall. The company says mercenary spyware operations devote substantial resources to targeting particular individuals, often because of their profession or public role.

threat notification guidance, its warnings reflect high confidence that a user has been targeted, although detection cannot provide absolute certainty. Apple withholds details about how it identifies attacks to prevent operators from adapting their techniques, and its notifications do not attribute responsibility to particular attackers or regions.

title: Apple Says HomeView Sets New Record in Design-Focused Interview
content:
TechRadar's Jacob Krol interviewed Apple's Vice President of Hardware Engineering Matthew Costello about Apple's all-new HomeView smart home display, which is available starting today. The discussion was largely focused on the HomeView's design, with Costello touching on the device achieving a display-related record for Apple products.


Specifically, the HomeView's display brightness can automatically go down to just 0.3 nits, which is a record low for any Apple product. This ultra-low brightness makes the HomeView especially ideal for a bedside table at night. 

"I really love the fact that this is the lowest light performance we've ever engineered into a product, so it's down to 0.3 nits," said Costello.

"So officially, I represent the most dim product ever inside of Apple," he quipped.

For comparison, some other Apple products like the latest iPhones and iPad mini are advertised as having a minimum 1-nit display brightness.

HomeView's maximum display brightness is 500 nits.

Unsurprisingly, Costello said the HomeView is designed for the home (truly shocking) and Siri AI.

"It really was constructed around Siri," he said. 

"We really custom-built this user interface for the home, so the apps and experiences that matter most in the home setting are really front and center," he added.

"There's no logging in, logging out, which is super cool. It recognizes you and your information, and when you step away, it's gone."

content:
Macworld





Whether you’re a Mac desktop or MacBook owner, there’s nothing quite like finding that keyboard that fits perfectly within your setup.
A keyboard, just as with picking the best mice for Mac, is a very personal choice. After all, you’re likely to be pressing its various keys and twirling its dials for hours each day, and that makes getting the investment right all that much more important.
Best Mac Keyboards fully tested
We have all sorts of Mac keyboards in this round-up, including Apple’s default Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and the cheaper, and still-on-sale Magic Keyboard. We have some keyboards with customizable keys and dedicated apps, and wired keyboards (for those fed up with searching for new batteries every few weeks) as well as ergonomic solutions to help you avoid RSI, and some pretty stylish offerings that give Apple a run for its money.
We also look at Hall Effect options that use magnetic sensors to detect key presses, full-size offerings and compact board. Here are our favorite keyboards for Mac users, many of which cost a lot less than Apple’s. Read on to find the Mac compatible keyboard that’s best for you.
You can also use Bluetooth keyboards with iPads, so expect to see some good options here if you are an iPad user, or take a look at our Best iPad Keyboards roundup.

Apple sells four models of its Magic Keyboard, and some are more magical than others despite looking similar. There are two sizes (one with numeric keypad and navigation keys, and a smaller, more portable model without these extra keys). If your desk space is limited or you often travel with your keyboard, the 11-inch version makes more sense than the 16.5-inch keyboard.
Keyboard type: Slim
Size options: Compact, Full
Colors: White, Black (full-size only)
Aside from size, the two different models are differentiated by the inclusion of a Touch ID key, which works only with Macs that have an M-series Apple Silicon processor (post 2020). If your Mac is old enough to still be running an Intel chip, go for the non-Touch ID model. Only the Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad is available with black keys; the others are all-white affairs. rather cheekily, Apple charges an extra 20 buck for the black version. Each is available in nearly 20 different language versions. English speakers can choose between US or British English.
The basic design of the two keyboards hasn’t actually changed that much, with the same slimline design and month-long battery life as their predecessors. At $149, the smaller Magic Keyboard With Touch ID is priced at quite a premium for the Touch ID sensor. And, like the standard Magic Keyboard, it feels rather cramped, with a small Space bar and cursor keys. The lack of ‘travel’ (the up and down movement of the keys as you press them) also makes the keyboard feel a bit lifeless for people who type a lot and need a bit more tactile feedback when they’re typing up a storm—they should consider one of the mechanical keyboards reviewed below. Then again, you might feel that your fingers have to do less ‘work’ compressing the key. 
The key feature of these keyboards, though, is the Touch ID sensor, which sits by the F12 button on the top row of Function keys. This works just like the Touch ID sensors on the MacBook. You’ll see a Touch ID panel appear in System Preferences when you first connect the keyboard. This allows you to store up to three fingerprints, which you can use to unlock your Mac, or to make secure payments on the Apple Store, or other online stores that support Apple Pay.
There are a few other new features as well, including an Emoji command on the Fn key in the bottom-left corner of the keyboard, which displays the Emoji viewer panel so that you can quickly add emojis to any document or message that you’re typing. There are new Function commands too, for activating Spotlight, Dictation and Do Not Disturb.
As always, the larger version of the keyboard is even more expensive ($179 white, $199 black) but the numeric keypad will be useful for people who do a lot of number crunching at work. There’s more room to provide a larger Space bar too, and larger navigation keys. Even so, the thin keyboard panel means that the keys still feel a bit lifeless, so business users and budding novelists may prefer to look at one of the larger and more solidly built keyboards available from other manufacturers reviewed here.
Save money by checking Amazon for: Smaller Apple Magic Keyboard with Touch ID (U.S. and U.K.); Apple Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad (U.S. and U.K.). For the cheaper Apple Magic Keyboard without Touch ID: Small (U.S. and U.K.); with Numeric Keypad (U.S. and U.K.). To further complicate your choice, Amazon still sells versions with a Lightning rather than USB-C charging port. We have linked here to just those that charge with USB-C.

It’s hard to keep up with Logitech’s ever-growing MX range of keyboards, but the Logitech MX Keys S For Mac ($129.99 / £109.99) is its top-of-the-range wireless keyboard, priced at $109.99/£109.99. Its slimline, low-profile design is very smart and attractive, and available in either Space Gray or Pale Gray. It’s the most solidly built Mac keyboard we have tested, and is capable of surviving some heavy-handed typing when it needs to.
The MX Keys S For Mac is significantly cheaper than Apple’s Magic Keyboard (from $179/£179), but also a lot more versatile, as it includes a dedicated set of buttons that allow you to pair it with three separate devices, including Macs, iPads, Windows PCs, and even Linux and Chrome devices. It does, like all non-Apple keyboards, lack the Magic Keyboard’s Touch ID key.
Look for the “For Mac” model as it offers a Mac dedicated layout. The Command Key is the giveaway when you want to ensure you have the regular Mac keyboard layout. There are different models for U.S. and U.K. layouts, too—which you don’t get with the Satechi keyboards.
The original MX Keys was launched a few years ago, so this updated MX Keys S includes a number of new features, such as Function keys that can be used to activate dictation on your Mac, open the emoji menu, or mute/unmute your microphone for video-calls. The backlighting has been improved too, automatically reacting as you first move your hands onto the keyboard, and adjusting to suit the ambient light in the room around you. The backlight does drain the battery though—the keyboard can last for up to five months if you’re not using the backlight, but this drops to around 10 days if you have the backlight on all the time.
You can use the MX Keys S with any Mac, and it will work like a standard keyboard with a row of Function keys that control settings such as brightness and volume, or activating Exposé. However, Logitech also provides an app, called Options+, which requires macOS 12 or later. This allows you to reprogram the various Function keys to perform different tasks. It can also be configured to work with specific apps such as Photoshop or Premiere, which makes it a particularly good option for professional users who want to speed up work in their key apps. The app has also been updated for the MX Keys S, adding a new Smart Actions feature that works a bit like Apple’s Shortcuts, by allowing you to record a series of actions that can be triggered using a single key.

How to pick the best keyboard 
Choosing the right keyboard is a personal decision that can significantly impact your daily comfort and productivity, whether you’re typing, gaming, or doing creative work. Key factors to consider include the keyboard’s primary use, its physical design, and the technology inside its keys.
Before diving into specific models, consider what you need from a keyboard. Your choice will depend on a combination of feel, features, and function.
Typing Experience and Comfort: The feel of the keys under your fingers is one of the most critical aspects. This includes key travel (the distance a key moves when pressed), the force required to register a keystroke, and the overall sound and tactile feedback. Some users prefer the deep, satisfying feedback of mechanical keyboards, while others favor the quiet, low-profile feel of membrane or scissor-switch models. Ergonomics also play a huge role; features like an adjustable typing angle, a built-in wrist rest, or even a split layout can help prevent discomfort and repetitive strain injuries.
Size and Layout: Keyboards come in various sizes. Full-size layouts include a numeric keypad, which is essential for anyone who frequently works with numbers. More compact options, such as tenkeyless (TKL), 75%, and 65% layouts, omit the number pad to save desk space and are often preferred by gamers or those with smaller workstations. The layout also affects the size and placement of important keys like the Shift and arrow keys, which can impact your typing habits. Familiar with an Apple keyboard lay out? A PC layout is very different, with various keys located in different positions and the Command and Alt/Option key switched.
Connectivity and Compatibility: You’ll need to decide between a wired or wireless keyboard. Wired keyboards offer a reliable connection without battery concerns, while wireless models provide a cleaner, untethered setup. Many wireless keyboards can connect via Bluetooth or a 2.4GHz USB dongle/receiver, with some offering the ability to pair with and switch between multiple devices, which is great for multitasking across a laptop, tablet, and phone. Some find using a 2.4GHz receiver is more responsive than Bluetooth, so this is often favored by gamers. Many USB dongles, however, are USB-A, and there’s no USB-A port on any modern Apple product so you might need an adapter. Also, ensure the keyboard is compatible with your operating system, whether it’s macOS, Windows, or both. Some keyboards include swappable keycaps and a switch to toggle between layouts. 
Language: It goes without saying that if you will want a keyboard that matches the keyboard layout common in your country. Especially if you aren’t an English speaker. 
Customization and Special Features: Many modern keyboards, especially mechanical ones, offer extensive customization. This can range from remapping keys and creating macros to swapping out the physical keycaps and switches (hot-swapping). Other features to look for include backlighting (for typing in low light), dedicated media controls or volume knobs, and specialized software for adjusting settings.
Mechanical vs Membrane Keyboards
The most significant distinction in keyboard technology is between mechanical and membrane models. This choice fundamentally shapes the typing experience.
Mechanical Keyboards: Praised for their durability, tactile feedback, and customizability, mechanical keyboards feature an individual physical switch under each key. This construction provides a more precise and consistent feel, with switches rated for tens of millions of keystrokes . They are highly popular with typists and gamers alike.
Switch Types: The feel of a mechanical keyboard is determined by its switches. Common types include linear (smooth, no bump), tactile (a noticeable bump mid-press), and clicky (a bump accompanied by an audible click). Some advanced keyboards feature Hall Effect or magnetic switches, which use electromagnetic fields to actuate keys, offering adjustable actuation points and enhanced durability.
Customization: A major draw for mechanical keyboards is the ability to customize them. Many models are “hot-swappable,” meaning you can easily change the switches without soldering to achieve your desired typing feel . You can also replace the keycaps with different materials, colors, or profiles.
Membrane Keyboards: These are the most common type of keyboard, often found in laptops and budget-friendly desktop models . They use a rubber or silicone layer under the keys that registers a keystroke when pressed down. While quieter and more affordable, they often provide a “spongy” or less precise feel and have a shorter lifespan compared to their mechanical counterparts . However, some high-quality membrane keyboards use a “scissor-switch” mechanism, which adds stability and provides a firmer, more responsive feel, similar to many modern laptop keyboards.
Finding the right keyboard for your needs
A keyboard is a very personal choice, and there’s no single “best” option for everyone.
For Office Work and Typing: If you type for long hours, prioritize comfort and ergonomics. A full-size keyboard with a number pad can boost productivity . Mechanical keyboards with tactile switches are often favored for their satisfying feedback, but a high-quality, quiet scissor-switch keyboard like the Logitech MX Keys S is also an excellent choice for a general-purpose office keyboard and is much quieter.
For Gaming: Gamers often prioritize speed and responsiveness. Keyboards with low latency, a high polling rate, and features like adjustable actuation or “rapid trigger” mode can provide a competitive edge . Compact TKL or 75% layouts are popular because they leave more room for mouse movement. Linear switches are often preferred for their smooth, quick action.
For Creatives and Customization Enthusiasts: Creatives may benefit from keyboards with special features like programmable dials or macro keys, such as the Logitech Craft . For those who love to tinker, a hot-swappable mechanical keyboard from a brand like Keychron offers endless possibilities for customization, from the switches and keycaps to the case material and internal sound-dampening foam.
Ultimately, the best way to choose a keyboard is to understand your own preferences for feel, sound, and features. From there, you can explore the different types of keyboard layouts, learn about the nuances of mechanical switch types, or compare the benefits of wired versus wireless keyboards.

title: If your old printer stopped working with macOS 27, there’s an easy fix
content:
Macworld





Printers may be one of the most hated devices in tech, but even in 2026, they’re a necessary part of our setups. We need them for specific, usually time-sensitive tasks, and when they don’t work, it can be a major pain.
For a lot of Mac users upgrading to macOS 27 Golden Gate, including me, that’s exactly what happened. While we’re used to some things needing updates or permissions to work after updating to a new version of macOS, Golden Gate caused more problems than usual, and some of the devices that you’ve depended on for years might have suddenly stopped working—including some Brother and Canon printers. If you’re like me, it might take a few weeks to notice because, well, you’re probably not printing things all that often. But when you do, it’s important, and you need it to work.
You can try to find a newer driver, but depending on the age of your printer, there’s a good chance you won’t be able to find one that’s been updated in a while. And if you try deleting your printer and adding it as a new device, it probably won’t be found either.
The problem lies with Rosetta, the background process that automatically translates Intel-based apps for use with Apple Silicon. It’s been silently running in the background ever since macOS Big Sur on the first M1 Macs. However, Apple removed its installation with macOS 27 Golden Gate as it prepares for a world without Intel apps when macOS 28 arrives next year.
Since many printers stick around for years, some very popular models relied on Rosetta to communicate with Apple Silicon Macs. Without Rosetta, that can’t happen with an old Intel-based driver.
But there’s an easy fix. Rosetta actually still exists on your Mac; it just needs to be turned on. To do that, head over to the Terminal (Applications > Utilities) and type the following command: softwareupdate –install-rosetta
Then hit return. The app will ask you to agree to the software license agreement. Assuming you do, press the letter “A” and hit return again. It’ll take a moment to install, and your printer should work (though you might need to restart the job that failed). If that doesn’t work, restart your Mac.
The bad news is that unless Apple changes its mind, you’ll need to get a new printer or a different workaround when macOS 28 arrives next year. But until then, happy printing.

service health page says affected users may have trouble opening mailboxes through Outlook on the web, desktop, and mobile. Messages may also be delayed.

title: HomeView has one big problem: The iPad
content:
Macworld





HomeView is Apple’s new attempt to compete with Amazon and Google in the smart home market. It only arrived in stores today, but it’s already shaping up to be a hit. Its design, which is somewhat reminiscent of a smaller iMac G4, is cute, and it runs an operating system based on iOS. But HomeView’s biggest problem is that there’s already another Apple product that can do most of the same things.
The main purpose of HomeView is to function as a HomeKit hub. But because it’s an Apple device, it also comes with some of the company’s most popular apps preinstalled. It lets you answer FaceTime calls, play songs on Apple Music, or even check your calendar with Siri AI. All of this comes packed into a device that costs $299, not exactly cheap, but relatively affordable for a new Apple product in 2026. But when even the cheapest iPad can do everything HomeView does and more, Apple’s new smart home hub starts to seem quite expensive for what it does.
The iPad is already a great smart home display
Many Apple users had been eagerly awaiting the company’s first smart home hub. That’s no surprise, given the vast market for HomeKit accessories. But the thing is, iPads were already fulfilling that role for many users already in the Apple ecosystem without even realizing it. 
Think about most of the things you’re most likely to do with a HomeView — check the weather, control the lights, send a message, play music. You can already do all of these things with an iPad without having to buy a new device. In fact, many Apple users have already turned an old iPad into a de facto smart home display just by placing it on a stand.

				
					

				
			
The new OLED iPad mini has a bigger screen and more capabilities than the HomeView.

Roman Loyola/Foundry




Granted, there are important differences between the two. The iPad wasn’t designed to be a smart hub and lacks some of HomeView’s really useful features, such as an always-on display and private multi-user support. Still, in other areas, the iPad ends up being much more versatile. The iPad can run pretty much any app from the App Store, while there’s no mechanism for installing apps on HomeView. And even the iPad mini has a larger canvas than the HomeView for widgets.
In terms of design, the iPad also has some advantages. The entry-level model features an 11-inch screen, compared to the HomeView’s 7-inch screen. Plus, the iPad has a built-in battery, so you can move it freely around your home. With HomeView, you have to think about where to place it and leave it there. 
Not only that, but you need to decide whether you want HomeView with its base or wall mount — there’s no way to switch between the two. With the iPad, you can. Sure, the HomeView has better speakers and a design that looks nicer sitting on a kitchen counter. But is that really worth giving up everything else?
The things HomeView does best
To be fair, it’s not that HomeView doesn’t have any benefits over the iPad. The first is Apple Intelligence — if you buy the cheapest iPad available today, it lacks even the most basic of Apple’s native AI features. HomeView is powered by the A18 chip from the iPhone 16, so it works with Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. It can answer more complex questions and even pull contextual information from your iPhone. The entry-level iPad, on the other hand, is still stuck with the old Siri. However, it’s only a matter of time before the base-model iPad gets a chip capable of running Siri AI.
But there’s another feature that might be even more important: multi-user support. Unlike the iPad, which was designed to be a personal device, HomeView can be used by up to six people in the same household. This is a must-have feature if you don’t want other people in your house snooping on your messages or photos. 
HomeView uses a Face ID-like facial recognition system to display each user’s personal data. Each person has their own Home Screen, widgets, and app content. From that perspective, HomeView makes a lot more sense as a smart hub than the single-user iPad.

				
					

				
			
HomeView’s biggest advantage is its app-less simplicity and muilti-user support

Foundry




HomeView vs. iPad: Which one to choose?
Don’t get me wrong, I do like the idea of the HomeView. It’s a great addition to Apple’s ecosystem, especially for those who have a lot of HomeKit stuff at home. Having a dedicated screen that anyone in the house can use is a nice feature that’s not really available on any other Apple device, and unlike an iPad, the HomeView is designed to be always available. You don’t have to worry about charging it, finding where you left it, or unlocking it every time you want to turn on the lights.
But I still think it’s hard to justify its price given all its limitations. Yes, an entry-level iPad costs $150 more, but it also does a lot more. It can serve as your smart home display and also function just like any other tablet, with a vast ecosystem of apps available. If you already have an old iPad at home, that’s even better. You just need to buy a stand for it. If not, a refurbished 11th-generation iPad costs almost the same as a HomeView.
I don’t think HomeView is a bad product, and it’s actually cool to see Apple getting more involved in the smart home market. But the first generation seems to have too many limitations for its price. So for most users like me, an iPad will likely remain the first choice for some people when it comes to their smart home hub.

title: Best MacBook Neo accessories: Chargers, hubs, stands and more
content:
Macworld





The MacBook Neo, Apple’s entry-level laptop officially announced in early March 2026, is a sensation, bringing the Mac to a whole new market with its low price but surprisingly powerful specs and features. For just $699 you get the full Mac experience in a premium aluminum 13-inch laptop with FaceTime HD camera, speakers, mic and two USB-C ports.
Compared to similarly priced Windows laptops and iPads with keyboards, the MacBook Neo offers superior build quality, performance, and storage capacity—for hundreds of dollars less than any previous Mac laptop.
We’ve outlined some of the small compromises that Apple has made to get to that ultra-keen price point, but most of these technicalities won’t bother the target audience at that great deal of a price tag.
That’s not to say that the MacBook Neo is perfect—otherwise why would the MacBook Air and Pro exist? For not a whole lot of extra outlay you can make the MacBook Neo an even better product and part of your digital lifestyle with these accessories. Here we list some of our favorite Mac accessories that we think every MacBook Neo owner should purchase or at least put on their wish list.
MacBook Neo limitations and solutions
Here are some of the limitations of the MacBook Neo that you can solve with the accessories in this guide. 
Slow 20W charger: Buy a faster charger
Only two USB-C ports: Buy a USB-C hub
One slow 480Mbps port: Buy a USB-C hub
Single external display support: Buy a DisplayLink dock
Small screen for desk use: Buy an external screen

				
					

				
			
Satechi




Essential MacBook Neo accessory 1: A charger
Apple ships the MacBook Neo with a 20-watt (20W) Power Adapter (unless you’re in the U.K. or E.U., where–tough luck–you’ll get just a charging cable and no actual charger). At just 20W, it’s a pretty low-powered adapter to be honest. In fact, it’s now hard to find a charger rated that low, with 30W or 45W increasingly the minimum output.
If you’re in a hurry for power, you’ll want something more capable than Apple’s puny 20W adapter. While Apple doesn’t list fast charging in the Neo’s tech specs, in our own Neo charging tests we found it does charge faster when paired with a more powerful charger.
Charging speed is largely determined by power output. The more watts available, the faster a device can charge—up to its maximum supported input. For example, you can plug a 140W charger into an iPhone, but it won’t charge any faster than it would with a 35W adapter as the Neo’s max input is 30W. A 30W charger will be faster than the 20W but a little more powerful supply will get through any latency. We recommend at least a 35W charger. Better still, buy a much more powerful charger with multiple ports so you can charge more than just your Neo with it.
We’ve chosen two alternative chargers to consider: a compact 45W single-port model and a 65W multiport charger. For more options, see our roundup of the best USB-C chargers for MacBook for even more choice.

title: Can your Mac run macOS 27? Check the full compatibility list
content:
Macworld





Wondering which versions of macOS your Mac can run? Want to know if you can run macOS 27 Golden Gate? We’ve put together a macOS compatibility checker that will show you what Macs the different versions of macOS and Mac OS X support, so you can tell what version you should be running on your Mac if you want the latest features and security protections.
Read on to find out exactly which Macs are supported by each version of the Mac operating system.
Latest supported macOS version
macOS 27 Golden Gate arrived on September 14. 
Latest version: The latest update to Golden Gate is macOS 27.2.1, which arrived on November 9, 2026.
Supported Macs: All Apple silicon Macs, including the A18 Pro-powered MacBook Neo. Intel-powered Macs cannot run Golden Gate.
Latest security updates: Apple released macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.3, and macOS Sequoia 15.8.3 on November 9, 2026
Which version of macOS can my Mac run?
Apple releases a new version of the Mac operating system every year—but the newest version of the Mac operating system does not support every Mac. Each year more and more Macs fall off the compatibility list and are unable to be updated to take advantage of the latest features.
Here’s a simple table you can use to identify the version of macOS your Mac can run based on the year it was introduced. Note there are some exceptions where only certain models are compatible with a macOS version. For more details of specific models check the sections later on in this article.

How long do Macs last?
Can I install an older OS on my Mac?
Officially, the operating system that was available on your Mac at the time that you bought it is the oldest version of macOS that can run on that Mac. It’s likely that an older OS won’t include the necessary drivers for the hardware on newer Macs. For this reason, it is unlikely that you will be able to install an older version of macOS on a new Mac—but you can take a look at how to install old versions of macOS or OS X for other Macs. Owners of Macs with M-series chips (sometimes referred to as Apple Silicon) won’t be able to run older versions of macOS that weren’t designed for Apple Silicon Macs which use a different architecture, known as ARM, instead of x86.
But it may not just be a case of wanting to know if your Mac can run the newest operating system. You might also want to know if it is possible to downgrade your Mac to an older version of macOS and need to know the oldest version of macOS you can use. You’ll also find that information below. You can also see a complete list of all the different versions of macOS and Mac OS X. Not sure which Mac you own? Check our article about how to identify your Mac.

The 4th-generation ‌Apple TV‌ 4K ships with tvOS 27.0, and users are prompted to update it to tvOS 27.2 during the setup process.

Apple hasn't said when tvOS 27.2.1 will be released with ‌Siri‌ AI for older ‌Apple TV‌ 4K models, but it could come as soon as Friday.

title: Apple Explains How HomeView Keeps Camera Data Private
content:
Apple today shared an in-depth look at how it's using Secure Exclaves to protect camera and microphone data on the HomeView, iPhone 18 Pro, and other products.


Apple describes Secure Exclaves as compartmentalized runtimes that process camera and microphone data while isolated from the rest of the operating system. Data processed in Secure Exclaves is not available to the rest of the OS, apps, or Apple, but processing can take advantage of the full application processor. Secure Exclaves power sensitive features involving video and audio feeds:

 	
HomeView - The HomeView uses facial and voice recognition to identify up to six people in a home. The exclave also protects the LED camera indicator on the device.

 	
Siri Recap and Live Rewind - Record ambient sound for conversation recaps or to caption the last 15 seconds of someone speaking.

 	
iPhone 18 Pro/iPhone Duo - Protects the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌, Pro Max, and Duo on-screen camera and microphone indicators. Also works with "Hey Siri" to protect voice data.

 	
MacBook Neo - Protects the MacBook Neo camera indicator.


Apple uses the HomeView as an example of how Secure Exclaves work. The device performs passive minimal visual processing continually to detect whether a person is in its field of view. The HomeView sends a continuous stream of camera frames to a camera exclave, which works alongside a person recognition exclave with face and voice recognition models and an identity database. When a person comes into view, the camera exclave detects the person and lets the main OS know that a person may be present, but no image data leaves the Secure Exclave. An audio exclave does the same thing with audio.

The person recognition exclave matches face and voice prints against the identity database of enrolled users, giving a confidence score. The OS gets the person identifier, position, and confidence level, but not any of the actual audio or video. These simple signals are used to activate personal features like Calendar and Messages that depend on identity, with raw sensor data discarded.

Secure Exclaves came about because Apple needed a secure option for ambient video and microphone monitoring, with the groundwork laid starting in iOS 18. Apple devices use indicators for situations where the camera and microphone are actively engaged, but Apple says they weren't ideal for ambient sensing because they would be on all the time. Always-on lights wouldn't give users a way to distinguish between background sensing and active audio and video recording.

There are two modes for a Secure Exclave: ambient mode and active mode. In ambient mode with no indicator, a sensor can respond to triggers, but it only shares small amounts of metadata with the rest of the system. In active mode, full sensor data is given to the operating system, and an indicator informs the user that the system has audio and video access.

Apple has long used indicators, but they are now backed by Secure Exclaves. Secure Exclaves make sure an indicator is active before data is allowed to be transferred from the exclave to the rest of the OS.

title: Nvidia’s CEO scandal could have major repercussions at Apple Park
content:
Macworld





If you haven’t heard, Nvidia is looking for a new CEO to replace Jensen Huang following a scandal involving an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. We won’t get into the particulars (you can read all about it here), but since Nvidia is perhaps the most important chip manufacturer in the world thanks to AI, it’s going to need a new permanent CEO as soon as possible. Among the list of candidates are your typical Nvidia internal executives, as well as several from outside the company.
Here’s why Apple fans should care: Apple’s Chief Hardware Officer Johny Srouji has been named by Bloomberg as a top candidate for Nvidia’s CEO position. Citing Srouji’s leadership of the “most successful in-house silicon programs in the industry,” Bloomberg notes that Srouji’s “track record gives him deep credibility on chip design, product integration and long-term technology roadmaps.”
The list also includes Nvidia CFO Colette Kress, who was named interim CEO following Huang’s resignation, Nvidia VP Ian Buck, AMD CEO Lisa Su, Micron Technology CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, and others. To be clear, these are all major players in the tech world with deep knowledge of the chip industry.
What’s less clear from the report is whether the list of candidates was obtained from an Nvidia source or simply some educated speculation by the Bloomberg reporters, but it makes sense that Srouji would be considered.  A longtime exec and face of Apple’s keynotes, Srouji has led Apple’s chip efforts from the start, including the development of the first A4 chip in the iPhone and M1 chips in Macs. 
Apple’s A-series chips are a major reason why the iPhone continues to be the best-performing smartphone in the industry, and the transition of Mac hardware from Intel chips to Apple silicon has been a huge success that has contributed to the Mac’s growing market share. They continue to set the standard for mobile and desktop processors, and have upended the consumer chip industry as manufacturers scramble to compete.
Srouji was named Apple’s Chief Hardware Officer earlier this year, at the same time Tim Cook announced his retirement as Apple CEO. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported in December 2025 that Srouji seriously considered leaving Apple, and the speculation is that the promotion to CHO was part of an effort to keep him at the company. “I don’t plan on leaving anytime soon,” Srouji reportedly said to his staff in response to Gurman’s report. But that was then, and being handed the reins of one of the largest companies in the world could cause him to reconsider.
Less likely to be a candidate is Tim Cook, who stepped down as CEO on September 1. His name wasn’t included in the Bloomberg report but President Donald Trump posted on his Truth Social network that Cook is the “only one man” who could fill Jensen’s shoes as CEO. “A Legend replaces a Legend!” he wrote.

title: Mac malware doesn't need a security flaw when users do the work
content:
Bitdefender's latest Mac threat report shows adware gaining ground as attackers increasingly use browser scams to trick users into bypassing Apple's security protections.

MacBook Air M5
Bitdefender's September 2026 macOS Threat Landscape Report analyzes more than 1.5 billion security events collected between August 2025 and July 2026. Excluding web and document threats, adware rose from 22.6% of detections in the previous report to 34.4%.
Trojans remained the largest category at 45.2%, down from 51.8%. Potentially unwanted apps also fell from 25.3% to 20.4%.
The shift reflects the growing prominence of malicious ads, browser redirects, and deceptive software installers that trick users into compromising their Macs.

title: Apple’s rumored smart glasses were just confirmed by a supplier. Whoops!
content:
Macworld





Apple, as a general rule, is extremely secretive about its unreleased products. But that rule doesn’t always apply to its supplier partners, whose PR strategies may not be quite as strict or polished. And sure enough, one of those companies now appears to have revealed, quite blithely and deliberately, the existence of Apple’s rumored smart glasses project.
The Changzhou-based firm Quick Intelligent Equipment this week made its Q3 2026 earnings report. And according to a Chinese-language article by People’s Finance News (via MacRumors), this report contained the explosive claim that the supplier’s revenues were bolstered by working with Apple on a new set of “smart earphones” and a pair of AI glasses. Neither of those projects has yet been announced by Apple, and therefore neither of them has officially existed… until now.
“The company has participated in Apple’s AI glasses and new smart earphone projects, which will help drive related businesses such as precision welding assembly and machine vision inspection,” the report claims (via Google Translate), without appearing to realise how much trouble someone could get in for leaking that information anonymously, let alone publishing it in a public financial disclosure. (Quick Intelligent Equipment didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.)
Granted, Apple itself leaked video of a new set of camera-equipped AirPods this summer, which is likely what the “smart earphones” refers to. But the AI glasses are simultaneously a bigger deal and a better-kept secret, and John Ternus will be very frustrated if a supplier really has spilled the beans in this bizarrely shameless way.
Apple has already entered the mixed-reality wearables business with the Vision Pro, but the company hopes at some point to launch something more portable and appealing to mainstream users. Widely referred to by external media as Apple Glass, and reportedly known at Apple Park by the codename N50, Apple’s first set of smart glasses are expected to be ready for a launch as soon as the first quarter of 2027. We’ll all have to pretend to be surprised.

title: Nintendo to End 'Sign in With Apple' Support in January
content:
Nintendo will stop allowing users to sign in to their Nintendo Account with an Apple or Google account on January 26, 2027, the company has announced.


Users will also no longer be able to create a Nintendo Account through either service. Nintendo has not explained why it is removing the options, but notes that the exact cutoff could be delayed depending on the progress of its system updates.

After the change, users will need to sign in with their Nintendo Account email address or Sign-In ID and password, or use a passkey. Nintendo says users who are already signed in on a device may not need to sign in again immediately.

Nintendo Account login page to request a reset email.

Sign in with Apple may have an Apple-generated relay address registered with Nintendo. Messages sent to that address are forwarded to their personal inbox. Nintendo advises anyone who can no longer access their registered email address to contact its support team.

We’ve rounded up the best MagSafe, Qi2, Qi2.2 25W, and MagSafe-compatible magnetic chargers, from the plain pad to multi-functional stands (up to six devices charged), and even the most colorful—from snap-on chargers and modular stands to foldable power banks and full charging desk mats.
Apple’s MagSafe technology, supported by all models of iPhone since the iPhone 12 (except the iPhone SE and 16e), presents a more efficient way of wirelessly charging compatible iPhones. MagSafe is the ring of magnets around the iPhone’s internal charging coil that senses compatible accessories and magnetically snaps securely into the most efficient charging position with the right accessories. With MagSafe, you’re less likely to wake up to find your phone wasn’t correctly placed on the wireless charger so didn’t charge at all!
Testing the best for you
We have tested a lot of magnetic chargers—MagSafe, Qi2 and Compatible—and here inform you which one will work best for you. There are simple magnetic wireless chargers, multi-device chargers for iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods, travel chargers, car chargers and more. 
Best simple MagSafe chargers
Best 2-in-1 MagSafe chargers
Best 3-in-1 MagSafe chargers
Best 4-in-1 MagSafe Chargers
Best travel MagSafe chargers
Best MagSafe charging stands with power banks
Best MagSafe car charger
Best wireless charging desk mat
Best wireless charging sleeve
Offering up to 25W power output in the right configuration, MagSafe charging is much faster than basic 7.5W magnetic wireless charging. The similar magentic Qi2 standard, supported by the iPhone 13-18 families (and unofficially the iPhone 12 but strangely not the latest 16e) offers similar 15W speed charging. Qi 2.2, also known as Qi2 25W, meets MagSafe at 25W for iPhone 16/17/18 series.
MagSafe or Qi2 certification
Apple certifies MagSafe accessories to ensures that the output charging is 15W for most iPhones, and up to 25W for iPhone 16 and later (with Apple’s latest MagSafe charger or chargers certified for Qi2.2 25W). Non-certified magnetic but “MagSafe-compatible” chargers are usually just 7.5W with a ring of magnets to hold your phone in place. Certified MagSafe chargers also have a single-wire NFC antenna that allows the iPhone to identify the device and a built-in magnetometer to prevent compass interference while you are using your iPhone while it’s charging.
In our tests, 15W MagSafe and Qi2 chargers are evenly matched for charging speeds. 7.5W MagSafe compatible chargers, as you might expect, take around twice as long—certainly in the early stages of charging. But don’t rule out 7.5W chargers as they are often high quality, nearly always noticeably cheaper and just take a while longer to fully charge an iPhone. The king of the hill is Apple’s new MagSafe charger and chargers based on the new Qi2.2 25W technology that are definitely faster at 25W, but only with iPhone 16 or later.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Simple vs multi-device magnetic chargers
The most basic form of MagSafe or magnetic charger is the simple pad that latches on to the compatible iPhone. Some pads feature a pop-out arm so the iPhone can be propped up while charging. There are also products that can simultaneously charge an iPhone plus other Apple devices, such as an Apple Watch or wireless AirPods charging case. Note that the AirPods case must be of the wireless variety, and the original 2016-19 AirPods case lacked this functionality. The base of a multi-charger could also be used to charge a second iPhone but mostly not magnetically and at 5W rather than 7.5W, 15W, or 25W. Also see our round up of the Best Apple Watch chargers and stands.
Best simple MagSafe chargers
A simple MagSafe charging pad is the cheapest route to wireless iPhone charging. If you are going to the bother of connecting this product to a wall charger, why not just use a Lightning (iPhone 14 or earlier) or USB-C (iPhone 15 and up) cable direct to the iPhone? You can fast-charge an iPhone to 50% battery in under 30 minutes using a cable and just over that using a 25W charger, while it takes around 45-50 minutes to wirelessly charge iPhone from 0 to 50% using even 15W MagSafe.
That said, there are interesting options to choose from. After these we’ll look at more multi-functional MagSafe chargers.

Apple’s latest version of this charger offers fast 25W charging speed with iPhone 16 and later (15W for older iPhones). It also added a 2-meter length option for $10/£10 more, which is most welcome. At least a 30W USB-C power adapter is required for 25W charging. In our tests using the Apple MagSafe Charger we wirelessly powered up an iPhone 16 Pro from 0% to 50% in just over 30 minutes.

The premium-quality, vegan leather Journey NEXA laptop sleeve bills itself as a “4-in-1”, and it certainly is multi-functional.
As well as protecting your laptop during travel, it includes two wireless chargers (one MagSafe compatible at 7.5W; one 5W for AirPods or a second phone) and can work as both a desk mat and mousepad to free your workspace of clutter.
The most recent NEXA Lift model features an iPhone charger that raises into an adjustable stand.
While it comes with a USB-C cable, you’ll need to add your own charger (check our roundup of the best iPhone chargers) to connect with the USB-C port in the sleeve. Alternatively you can charge the MacBook itself while it sits protected in the sleeve—for this you’ll need a more powerful MacBook charger.

							
		
Why wireless?
Wireless charging is convenient and fine for situations when you don’t need a super-fast recharge, although the latest 25W wireless chargers are getting close to the power and therefore speed you’ll get from charging via a cable
If you’re leaving your home in 20 minutes and need as much juice as possible, plug in a cable (USB-C for iPhone 15 or later, or Lightning for earlier iPhones) into a USB-C charger (of at least 30W) to power up an iPhone faster than wireless. With 25W wireless chargers you can simply place your iPhone on and know you should be able to charge it to 50% in around 30 minutes.
Wireless charging is less wearing than constantly inserting a cable into your phone, and more reliable as that vulnerable cable port can fill with fluff and dust after all the time spent in your trouser pocket or bag and it’s one of the most common reasons that an iPhone refuses to charge even when connected with a cable. It’s easy to clean with a toothpick (but please do it softly!) but will affect most of us at some time. Read our tips about how to clear dirt and fluff from your iPhone’s charging port.
Wireless charging isn’t affected by the build-up of dust and fluff in the phone port and is also less vulnerable to oxidation and corrosion.
With wireless, you don’t have to remember to run around trying to find who’s taken your charging cable, and it’s certainly a lot neater.
Of course, wireless charging is not really wireless, unless you are using a portable magnetic power bank. The magnetic charger is still connected by a cable to your wall charger; it’s just the connection to the phone that is properly wireless.
What else you need
Some magnetic chargers come with their own wall charger, but most require you to add your own. Apple recommends at least a 20W USB-C power adapter (wall-socket charger) and we agree unless your charger supports 25W wireless charging, in which case go with at least a 30 USB-C charger or higher if it’s a 2-in-1 or 3-in-1 multi-device charger.
We have tested the best iPhone wall chargers to help you choose a recommended solution.

title: Apple Home Collection: Select Accessories Available to Order This Friday
content:
Apple today announced that select Apple Home Collection accessories will be available to order starting Friday, November 13, with availability beginning in December. Apple did not say exactly which accessories can be ordered tomorrow, so stay tuned.


Introduced alongside Apple's new HomeView smart home hub last month, the Apple Home Collection is a new lineup of smart home accessories that LG and Schneider Electric designed in collaboration with Apple. There are indoor and outdoor cameras, thermostats, temperature sensors, a video doorbell, and a door lock.


 	
LG Video Doorbell ($249.95) - The Video Doorbell has dual cameras that capture views of visitors and packages. The front camera has a 2.5K resolution and the bottom camera is full HD resolution. It has a built-in spotlight and a chime that plays through HomeView, HomePod, or HomePod mini.

 	
LG Outdoor Cam ($299.95) - The Outdoor Cam has low-light color night vision and can be angled in multiple positions.

 	
LG Indoor Cam ($199.95) - The Indoor Cam has a privacy-preserving feature that allows it to tilt up when people are in the home so it's not recording, and down when people leave for keeping an eye on the home. The tilt function works based on geofencing, but can also be controlled in the Home app or manually.

 	
LG Floodlight Cam ($399.95) - The Floodlight Cam has dual floodlights that activate when motion is detected and low-light color night vision.

 	
LG Smart Deadbolt Lock ($349.95) - The lock has Ultra Wideband and can unlock automatically when the homeowner approaches, with no tap required. It also supports unlocking via PIN or a hidden backup key slot, and there is detection for whether the door is opened, closed, or has been tampered with. The doorbell and lock can work together as one, letting users see who is at the door and unlocking it if needed.

 	
LG Thermostat ($199.95) - The thermostat supports Adaptive Temperature and in the U.S., heating and cooling can be activated during lower-cost periods for users with a compatible utility plan. The thermostat can read temperature and humidity across multiple rooms using separate temperature and humidity sensors. Sensors are priced at $39.95.

 	
Schneider Electric Thermostat ($199.95) - Also supports Adaptive Temperature and can be used with temperature and humidity sensors. Sensors are priced at $39.95.

For more details about the accessories, read our previous coverage.
